source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 2 · lesson 5. Exercises reused from the lesson.
topic: Made of light, always obeying Allah

learn.en: The Arabic word for angel is malak; the plural is malā'ikah. Allah created them from light.
learn.title: Made of light

learn.en: We cannot see them, but we know they are there because the Prophet ﷺ told us.
learn.title: Unseen

learn.en: The angels are Allah's servants. They always obey Him and never disobey.
learn.title: Always obeying

learn.en: Angel Jibreel brought the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and Allah's messages to many prophets before him.
learn.title: Jibreel

learn.en: Every one of us has two angels who write down everything we do and say, good and bad. Mika'eel, Israfeel and Malik are angels too.
learn.title: Two angels with us

learn.en: “They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them but do what they are commanded.” (Qur'an 66:6)
learn.title: From the Qur'an

quiz.en: What is the Arabic word for angels?
True or false? The angels sometimes disobey Allah.

think.q: Two angels write down everything you say and do. What would you like them to write about you today?
think.a: Kind words, helping at home, praying on time…

parents.summary: Angels (malāʾika) are made of light and always obey Allah; Jibreel brought the Qur'an; two angels record our deeds.
parents.tip: At bedtime, ask: what good did your angels write today?
